# SurveyBeat

Cloudflare-only Effect app. One Durable Object per Organization is the system of record; D1 holds only the global index and auth/email bookkeeping, never survey content. Two Workers serve the app/API (`MainWorker`) and the answer page's submission path (`SubmissionWorker`).

Read `SPEC.md` (authoritative spec), `GLOSSARY.md` (domain vocabulary), and `docs/adr/` (binding decisions) before changing behavior. `docs/infra.md` covers stages, WorkOS sign-in, email, and observability.

## Ground rules

- Use glossary terms exactly: Pulse (not Survey), Person (not User), Round (not instance), Submission (not Response). Do not drift to the "avoid" synonyms.
- If a change contradicts an ADR, say so and add a new ADR under `docs/adr/`; never silently override one.
- Issues and specs live in GitHub issues (`gh`); conventions are in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`. Commit subjects name the release slice, e.g. `R1 03: ...`.
- Privacy invariants are release blockers (SPEC §7): anonymous Submissions store no Person and no time (ADR 0005), comments are redacted at store time (ADR 0009), and every shown aggregate obeys the minimum group size (ADR 0004).

## Commands (from the repo root)

Node 24 (`.node-version`) and pnpm 12.18.0 are pinned.

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm typecheck          # tsc -b with project references
pnpm typecheck:effect   # @effect/tsgo diagnostics; CI runs this first
pnpm lint               # oxlint --type-aware
pnpm format             # oxfmt; CI runs format:check
pnpm test               # Vitest "unit" project only
pnpm test:privacy       # Vitest "privacy" project only; NOT part of pnpm test
pnpm test <path>        # one file, e.g. pnpm test packages/domain/src/people/SignIn.test.ts
pnpm --filter @surveybeat/web build
```

CI runs `typecheck:effect`, `typecheck`, `format:check`, `lint`, `test`, then the web build; the privacy suite is a separate required job. There is no root `dev` script: `pnpm --filter @surveybeat/web dev` serves the UI only, and the app calls the API at `window.location.origin`. Exercise sign-in and end-to-end flows on a deployed stage.

## Layout and boundaries

- `packages/domain` — Effect schemas and services by concept (`people/`, `email/`); depends only on `effect`.
- `packages/api` — the `HttpApi` declaration shared by the Worker and the typed web client; depends on `domain`.
- `packages/cloudflare` — all Cloudflare adapters plus the `MainWorker` and `SubmissionWorker` entries; the only package that touches the Alchemy runtime.
- `apps/web` — one Vite project with two entries: the Foldkit app (`index.html`) and the plain-TypeScript answer page (`answer.html`).
- `packages/emails` — React Email templates and rendering. `packages/testing` — privacy harness. `infra` — Alchemy stack, scripts, Playwright e2e, privacy sweep. `tools/oxlint-plugin-surveybeat` — local lint rules.

## Toolchain traps

- Effect is 4.1.2, not 3.x. Import from `effect/Effect`, `effect/Schema`, `effect/http-api`, `effect/http/...`; there is no `@effect/platform` v3-style API here. Copy the import style from neighboring files.
- TypeScript 7 (native compiler) with `tsc -b`. A new package needs its own `tsconfig.json` and an entry in the root `tsconfig.json` references.
- Stricter than defaults: `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `verbatimModuleSyntax` (use `import type`), and relative imports carry explicit `.ts`/`.tsx` extensions.
- Lint bans `any` and type assertions (`as Foo`) outside `*.test.ts` (`consistent-type-assertions: never`). Decode with Effect Schema or use typed helpers instead.
- All user-facing text comes from `apps/web/src/messages/catalog.ts` or `packages/emails/src/messages/catalog.ts`; `no-literal-ui-text` fails otherwise. HTML shells must hold no visible text and an empty `<title>` (asserted in `messages.test.ts`). Plurals use `<base>.one`/`.other`.
- The lint plugin enforces the boundaries: `domain`/`api` may not import `cloudflare:*`, Alchemy, or Foldkit, and `apps/web/src/answer/**` may not import React, Base UI, Foldkit, or the HttpApi client.
- Keep the answer entry plain TypeScript within its budget (JS ≤ 10 KB gzip critical path, CSS ≤ 2 KB inline, HTML ≤ 8 KB); no framework, per ADR 0008.

## Tests

- Tests are colocated `*.test.ts`. A privacy test must be named `*.privacy.test.ts` or CI never runs it.
- Use `@effect/vitest` (`it.effect` for Effect programs).
- Adapter tests use `@alchemy.run/test`'s `Test.make({ dev: true })` against local workerd and are slow (deploy timeouts up to 240 s); run the single file you need.
- A new API endpoint must be classified in `packages/api/src/PrivacyRegistry.ts` or the package will not typecheck; `registry.privacy.test.ts` checks the runtime declaration too.
- End-to-end tests run only against a deployed stage: `E2E_BASE_URL=https://pr-<n>.app.surveybeat.app pnpm test:e2e` (install Chromium once with `pnpm --filter @surveybeat/infra exec playwright install chromium`).

## Infra

- Every Cloudflare resource is declared in `infra/alchemy.run.ts`; no dashboard edits, no wrangler config.
- Run Alchemy from the repo root: the Organization DO migrations path (`packages/cloudflare/migrations`) is relative to the working directory. Build the web app first; the Main Worker serves `apps/web/dist`.
- `pnpm infra:deploy --stage dev-<name>` needs `WORKOS_API_KEY` and `WORKOS_CLIENT_ID` in the environment. Who may create an Organization is `infra/org-creation-allowlist.yaml`, per stage.
- Non-production stages never send real email; sends are recorded in D1's `captured_email`. Only `production` sends.
- The Submission Worker must keep every observability channel off. `pnpm check:observability --stage <stage>` reads the deployed settings back; the canary sweep proves no logs are kept. Stage scripts need `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`.
- New SQL migrations: numbered files in `packages/cloudflare/migrations` (Durable Object) or `packages/cloudflare/d1-migrations` (D1).

- [Cloudflare cf CLI](cloudflare-cf-cli.md) — authenticated cf CLI for SurveyBeat's Cloudflare account; discover commands with cf cli search
- [Wayfinder: always push and merge](wayfinder-always-push-merge.md) — push and squash-merge each resolved ticket's branch without asking

content.text:
## Changes

Added an Organization setting "AI processing" (off by default), modelled on `minimumGroupSize`. Nothing is committed.

- **Migration** `packages/cloudflare/migrations/0011_ai_processing.sql` (new, untracked): `ai_processing INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (ai_processing IN (0, 1))`. 0011 was the next free number.
- **`packages/cloudflare/src/SqlDirectory.ts`**: reads `ai_processing` into `aiProcessing` (boolean). The `SettingsUpdated` UPDATE writes both `minimum_group_size` and `ai_processing`.
- **`packages/domain/src/people/Directory.ts`**:
  - `DirectoryState.aiProcessing: boolean`.
  - `UpdateSettings` has optional `minimumGroupSize` and `aiProcessing`; absent means unchanged.
  - `decide` still requires `organization.updateSettings`, and resolves both values from state before emitting `SettingsUpdated`.
  - `applyChanges` and `settingsView` handle the new field.
- **`packages/domain/src/people/Team.ts`**: `OrganizationSettings` gains `aiProcessing: Schema.Boolean`.
- **`packages/api/src/index.ts`**: PATCH `/organization` payload has `minimumGroupSize` and `aiProcessing` as `Schema.optionalKey`. GET keeps its existing success schema, which now includes `aiProcessing` via `OrganizationSettings`.
- **`packages/cloudflare/src/DirectoryHandlers.ts`**: passes `aiProcessing` through. PrivacyRegistry is unchanged.
- **`apps/web/src/app/directory.ts`**: new "AI processing" panel below the minimum group size form, with a `checkboxField` and the help text.
- **`apps/web/src/app/App.ts`**:
  - Model fields `aiBusy` and `aiFailure`.
  - Messages `AiProcessingToggled` and `UpdatedAiProcessing`.
  - Command `UpdateAiProcessing`, which sends a PATCH with only `aiProcessing`.
  - After success it reloads settings with `GetSettings`.
- **`apps/web/src/messages/catalog.ts`**: the three `settings.aiProcessing.*` keys, with the text from the plan.
- **Tests**:
  - `packages/domain/src/people/Directory.test.ts`: a new `describe` block covering default off, admin-only changes, the `SettingsUpdated` payload, and independence from `minimumGroupSize`.
  - `apps/web/src/app/App.scene.test.ts`: a toggle test.
  - `aiProcessing: false` added to the fixtures in `App.story.test.ts`, `App.scene.test.ts`, `Editor.test.ts`, and `Results.privacy.test.ts`.

## Validation

- `pnpm typecheck`: **fails**, but only in `packages/cloudflare/src/auth/testing.ts` at lines 367, 379 and 678. Those `DirectoryState` literals lack `aiProcessing`. That file is owned by the other implementer, so I did not edit it. Everything else typechecks.
- `pnpm lint` (whole repo): one error, in `packages/cloudflare/src/ai/OpenRouterAiClient.test.ts:66` (`no-base-to-string`). That is the parallel implementer's file. Lint on my changed files is clean.
- `pnpm format` was run only on my files, not the repo, so the parallel implementer's in-progress files were not reformatted. `oxfmt --check` on those files passes. I did not run `pnpm format:check` repo-wide.
- `pnpm test` (unit): 563 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `packages/cloudflare/src/DirectoryApi.test.ts` "reads and sets the minimum group size", which returns 500 with `SchemaError: Expected boolean at ["aiProcessing"]`. Cause: that test runs against the in-memory Organization in `auth/testing.ts`, whose literals (see typecheck above) lack `aiProcessing`. It is the same blocker as the typecheck failure. Once those three literals get `aiProcessing: false`, this should pass, but I have not verified that.
- `pnpm test apps/web/src/app/App.scene.test.ts packages/domain/src/people/Directory.test.ts`: 51 passed, including the new tests.
- `pnpm test:privacy`: 34 passed.

## Notes

- **Blocker for the parallel implementer**: add `aiProcessing: false` to the three `DirectoryState` literals in `packages/cloudflare/src/auth/testing.ts`, at about lines 367, 379 and 678. Then typecheck and `DirectoryApi.test.ts` should pass.
- **Migration number clash risk**: I took `0011_ai_processing.sql`. If the parallel work also adds a DO migration, one of them needs renumbering.
- **Deviation from the plan**: `SettingsUpdated` carries the resolved `minimumGroupSize` and `aiProcessing` (both required), not an optional `aiProcessing`. `decide` fills the absent values from state inside the same transaction. The SQL stays a single UPDATE and the result is the same, and a `minimumGroupSize`-only update cannot reset `aiProcessing`.
- **API behaviour change**: `minimumGroupSize` is now optional in the PATCH payload, so an empty body is accepted as a no-op instead of a 400. Needed so the toggle can send only `aiProcessing`.
- **Double dispatch**: `checkboxField`'s `OnClick` fires twice per click (label and input). I added a guard so `AiProcessingToggled` is ignored while `aiBusy`. The existing Pulse editor checkbox has the same double dispatch, but it is harmless there because its toggles are idempotent.
- **PrivacyRegistry text**: `directory.updateSettings` still says `why: "sets the minimum group size; no content"`. It is accurate as a classification but now incomplete. I left it because the plan said to keep it.
- **Not run**: the adapter test `DirectoryApi.test.ts` was run only in the unit suite, and it fails for the reason above. I did not run `pnpm --filter @surveybeat/web build`.
